question: Dementia caregivers healed a small standard wound 24% slower than matched peers. Which follow-up best tests whether stress caused it?
options: Repeat with many more caregivers and peers
Ask caregivers to rate their own stress
Wound the same people when calm, then stressed
answer: Wound the same people when calm, then stressed. Caregivers may differ from peers in sleep, diet or health, and a bigger sample keeps all that. In 1998 the same team gave dental students identical mouth wounds in the summer holidays and three days before exams: exam-time wounds took 40% longer, about three days, to heal.
move: More of the same comparison cannot remove what the comparison itself hides.
trap: More people feels like stronger proof, but repeats the same comparison.
